Add `gunicorn` to `requirements.txt`, then start your Flask app with `gunicorn app:app --bind 0.0.0.0:$PORT` instead of `flask run`.

Gunicorn runs a master process plus several sync workers, so it handles real concurrent traffic and restarts a worker if one dies. Bind the port the platform assigns, set your secrets as env vars, and you're done.

Deploy Flask in 10 Minutes — Then the Reference You'll Keep

Quick thread 🧵
Add `gunicorn` to `requirements.txt`, then start your Flask app with `gunicorn app:app --bind 0.0.0.0:$PORT` instead of `flask run`.
Gunicorn runs a master process plus several sync workers, so it handles real concurrent traffic and restarts a worker if one dies.
Bind the port the platform assigns, set your secrets as env vars, and you're done.
